summary: Iter148 Phase 2.5 frontend review of useRememberedFilter, HelpTip, friendlyErrors and the 5 wired forms. Critical regression found in useRememberedFilter actor-key namespacing — it looks up the wrong localStorage keys and therefore always returns 'anon' for every signed-in user, which defeats the cross-portal isolation user mandate. Login flow also blocked end-to-end UI verification of HelpTip popovers / filter persistence reload / form submissions / friendly error rendering — the Safety sign-in button was visibly disabled and credentials did not produce a `masci.safety.token` after click (suggests client-side form-validation gate or rotated password). Static review of the three new utility files and the 5 wired pages otherwise looks clean.

ui_bugs.issue: CRITICAL: actor-key namespacing is broken. resolveActorKey() reads localStorage keys ['admin_token','safety_token','hr_token','pm_token','shop_token','dispatch_token','leadership_token'], but the app actually stores tokens under 'masci.admin.token','masci.safety.token','masci.hr.token','masci.pm.token','masci.shop.token','masci.dispatch.token'. None of the lookup keys ever match, so the function always falls through to 'anon'. Direct repro in the running app confirmed: after a real safety login, localStorage contains 'masci.safety.token' but actor-key resolves to 'anon'; only after manually setting 'safety_token' does it resolve to a hash. Effect: (1) Safety filters bleed into HR portal (and every other portal) — directly violates the iter148 cross-portal-isolation user mandate, (2) two users on the same shared device share remembered filters, (3) actor-key namespacing exists in name only. Fix: replace the lookup list with the real keys ['masci.admin.token','masci.safety.token','masci.hr.token','masci.pm.token','masci.shop.token','masci.dispatch.token','masci.directory.token'].

Could not authenticate end-to-end. Filled email=safety@mascigc.com / password=Safety123! and clicked Sign In; URL matched **/safety-portal** (because login page itself is /safety-portal/login), but no 'masci.safety.token' was stored — only 'masci.device.id' was present afterward. Sign-In button appears visibly grey/disabled in the rendered screenshot, suggesting form validation gate not satisfied OR the password listed in the review request (Safety123!) is stale vs the rotated one referenced in /app/memory/test_credentials.md (file notes Safety123! was rotated; no replacement value recorded). This blocked end-to-end verification of HelpTip popovers, filter persistence across reload, friendly error rendering, NewDailyReport smart-default pre-fill, and the export-button regression check. Please confirm current Safety credential or check why the Sign-In submit button is disabled in default state.

integration_issues.issue: Because resolveActorKey() always returns 'anon', any remembered filter written from the Safety portal lives at key prefix 'masci.ux.remembered.v1.anon.*' and will be read by the HR portal on next sign-in (HR also resolves to 'anon'). The user-mandate isolation guarantee does NOT hold in the current implementation.

rca of the issue: Root cause of cross-portal-bleed bug: code duplication of token-storage keys. The token names ('masci.admin.token','masci.safety.token',...) are defined locally in each lib/<portal>Auth.js file as a `const KEY = ...` string and never exported as a single source of truth. The author of useRememberedFilter.js (iter148) recreated the list from memory and used the older flat-name convention ('safety_token','admin_token',...) which is what those keys probably looked like in an earlier iteration before the 'masci.<portal>.token' rename. Because the keys silently miss, the function falls through to its 'anon' fallback for every user and no exception is thrown — the bug is invisible at runtime. Mitigation: (1) update the lookup list with the canonical 'masci.<portal>.token' names, OR (2) refactor each <portal>Auth.js to export its KEY constant and have useRememberedFilter import them so this can never drift again. Reproduction steps: open /safety-portal/login, run in DevTools console: `localStorage.setItem('masci.safety.token','x'.repeat(20))`, then evaluate the resolveActorKey logic (or check the prefix of any newly-written 'masci.ux.remembered.v1.*' key) — it will read 'anon' instead of a hashed actor key.
